China's CMOC secures funding support for buyback as China Merchants Bank pledges up to 1.8 billion yuan in dedicated loan
sum: CMOC (603993.SH) announced on November 12 that it has obtained a "Loan Commitment Letter" issued by the Shanghai Branch of China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., with a loan amount of up to 1.8 billion yuan (approximately $270.1 million), a term of 36 months, and funds earmarked for repurchasing the company's A-shares.

The loan provides a clear source of funding for the buyback plan CMOC previously disclosed. According to the announcement, the company held the 15th extraordinary meeting of its seventh board of directors on November 6, 2026, at which it deliberated and approved a proposal to repurchase A-shares through centralized bidding. Under the plan, total buyback funding ranges from 1 billion to 2 billion yuan (approximately $150.1 million to approximately $300.1 million), the repurchase price cap is 22.78 yuan per share, and the implementation period is within three months from the date of board approval. The repurchased shares are intended to safeguard company value and shareholder rights and interests.

In terms of scale, the 1.8 billion yuan loan facility committed by China Merchants Bank's Shanghai Branch covers 90% of the buyback plan's upper funding limit and also exceeds the lower bound of the repurchase amount. This means that even if the company implements the buyback at the maximum 2 billion yuan scale, most of the funding has already secured bank credit support.

CMOC is also listed in Hong Kong under the H-share code 03993.HK. Since the company's A-share buyback plan was launched, the market has focused on its funding sources and execution pace. The arrival of the bank's dedicated loan commitment letter further clarifies the funding arrangements for the buyback plan.

Against the industry backdrop, the practice of Chinese A-share listed companies using dedicated bank loans to implement buybacks has gradually increased in recent years. Such loans are typically tied to buyback plans, with the use of funds strictly restricted. For CMOC, the 36-month loan term is longer than the three-month buyback implementation window, leaving some room for fund allocation even after the buyback is completed.
Market participants believe that advancing the buyback plan alongside dedicated loan support helps convey to investors the company's assessment of its own value.

China CITIC Bank to launch pending-order feature for gold accumulation plan next Monday as Chinese banks jostle amid sharp gold price swings
sum: Gold prices have swung sharply since late October, yet Chinese commercial banks have been rolling out one "new feature" after another for their gold accumulation plans in the interim. China CITIC Bank (601998.SS) said in a Nov. 9 announcement that it expects to add a pending-order function to its personal Gold Accumulation Plan from Nov. 16, 2026, with the exact launch time subject to what is displayed on the trading page of the bank's app; the personal gold accumulation business agreement will be updated accordingly.

A pending order means an investor presets a price, quantity and validity period through the bank's electronic channels, and once gold prices hit the set conditions within that period, the system automatically completes the purchase or redemption. For ordinary investors, this amounts to handing the screen-watching to the system, saving the time spent tracking real-time quotes and, to some extent, reducing emotionally driven trades that chase rallies and dump on dips.

China CITIC Bank is not the first lender to launch the feature. Industrial Bank announced on June 2 this year that from June 8, 2026, its demand-deposit gold accumulation product would support pending-order purchases and pending-order redemptions; Bank of Nanjing announced on Oct. 22 that from Oct. 26 its personal gold accumulation business would add an entrusted pending-order function, with the business agreement revised in tandem. Checks show that China Construction Bank and China Merchants Bank have also introduced pending-order functions.

China CITIC Bank noted in its announcement that after the agreement is updated and before a customer signs the new agreement, the system will no longer support new purchase transactions, including real-time purchases and entrusted purchases; sell transactions (including real-time and entrusted sells) and existing regular investment plans will not be affected, subject to what the trading system displays. That means existing customers need to watch the signing timing so as not to disrupt subsequent position-building plans.
Zeng Gang, dean of the Tianfu Liyan Institute of Finance, cautioned that a "pending order" does not guarantee execution — if gold prices never touch the preset level, investors may miss the move.

China's optical module leader TFC Communication launches 150 million yuan buyback, all shares to be canceled
sum: On the evening of November 9, Shenzhen Stock Exchange-listed companies密集 disclosed buyback and shareholding increase plans, among which the buyback plan unveiled by optical module leader TFC Communication (300394.SZ) drew attention for its "full cancellation" feature. The company plans to use its own funds to repurchase part of its A-shares, with the buyback amount ranging from 100 million yuan to 150 million yuan (approximately $15.0 million to approximately $22.5 million) and a maximum repurchase price of 350 yuan per share; all repurchased shares will be canceled and registered capital reduced accordingly. As of the November 9 close, TFC Communication traded at 122.82 yuan per share, with a total market value of 133.98 billion yuan (approximately $20.1 billion).

Unlike most companies that use repurchased shares for equity incentives, TFC Communication explicitly plans to cancel all repurchased shares. With the maximum repurchase price set far above the current price, the plan is interpreted by the market as a move to directly boost earnings per share and transfer value to shareholders.

The same evening, PCB leader Wus Printed Circuit (002463.SZ) announced it plans to use its own funds or self-raised funds to repurchase part of its A-shares through centralized bidding, with a total buyback amount of no less than 500 million yuan and no more than 1 billion yuan (approximately $75.1 million to approximately $150.1 million), and a maximum repurchase price of 156.70 yuan per share. Fifty percent of the repurchased shares will be used for an employee stock ownership plan or equity incentives, and the other 50% to safeguard company value and shareholder rights. Wus Printed Circuit rose 5.31% that day to close at 77.1 yuan per share, with a total market value of 148.69 billion yuan (approximately $22.3 billion).

Wus Printed Circuit also disclosed a shareholding increase plan by its actual controller. Hepai Youlian Co., controlled by the Wu Ligan family, plans to increase its stake in the company using its own or self-raised funds within six months from the date of the announcement, with the increase amount no less than 20 million yuan and no more than 30 million yuan (approximately $3.0 million to approximately $4.5 million).

Sixteen Credit Card Units Shut Down in China This Year as Guangzhou Bank Sets Precedent With Full Withdrawal of Licensed Standalone Center
sum: The institutional landscape of China's credit card industry is contracting at an accelerating pace. As of Nov. 7, 16 credit card centers and their sub-centers have received approval from local financial regulatory bureaus to terminate operations this year, involving institutions including Bank of Communications, China Minsheng Bank, Ping An Bank, Huaxia Bank and Guangzhou Bank. At the same time, card issuance has declined for two consecutive years, standalone credit card apps are being shut down one after another, and departmental structures are being merged and adjusted — multiple signals pointing to the same trend: the credit card business is moving from a period of scale expansion into a phase of deepening its existing base.

By institutional distribution, joint-stock banks are the main force in this round of consolidation. Bank of Communications' Pacific Credit Card Center Chengdu sub-center is on the list; China Minsheng Bank had three credit card sub-centers approved for termination; Ping An Bank and Huaxia Bank each had two. Among city commercial banks, Guangzhou Bank has the most institutions involved: in addition to seven sub-centers, its head-office credit card center received approval on July 10 from the Guangdong bureau of China's National Financial Regulatory Administration to terminate operations and have its financial license canceled, with the existing credit card business, creditor-debtor relationships and contractual rights and obligations taken over by a newly established credit card department at the head office. This means China's first head-office-level credit card specialist center holding an independent financial license has been shut down entirely and transformed into an in-house department of the head office.

Institutional consolidation is only one side of the "slimming down." The People's Bank of China's "Overall Operation of the Payment System in the Second Quarter of 2026" shows that by the end of the second quarter, China had 677 million credit cards and combined credit-debit cards nationwide, down 10 million from the first quarter. At the end of 2024 the figure was 727 million, and at the end of 2025 it fell to 696 million — card issuance has declined for two consecutive years.

Hong Kong Stock Exchange: Hang Seng Index Edges Up 0.25% to 24,271.20 as Banks Offset Xiaomi Slide
sum: The Hang Seng Index gave up most of a strong opening rally on Monday 12 October 2026 but still closed 59.85 points higher, as banks and NetEase offset a 5.55% drop in Xiaomi and weakness in Hong Kong's technology sector.

The Hang Seng Index, the main benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, closed at 24,271.20 on Monday 12 October 2026, up 59.85 points or 0.25% from Friday's close of 24,211.35. Full-day turnover on the main board was HK$162.6 billion. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index also rose 0.25% to 8,168.57, while the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 0.67% to 4,169.57.

The shape of the session told a more cautious story than the headline gain. The index opened sharply higher at 24,434.93 and touched an intraday high of 24,455.95 in the first few minutes of trading, helped by early buying in Alibaba and NetEase. It then slid steadily through the morning, dropped to a low of 24,193.30 shortly after the lunch break, briefly below Friday's close, and recovered in the afternoon to finish modestly positive.

Banks and insurers provided the main support. China Merchants Bank rose more than 3%, and financial heavyweights helped the index hold its gains while technology shares diverged. Investors in Hong Kong were also reacting to a Saturday meeting in Beijing at which China's securities regulator signalled fresh support for the domestic stock market, although that message landed far less convincingly on the mainland, where the SSE Composite fell 0.43%.

The opening strength reflected Wall Street's record-setting week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq both posted record closes last week, and Hang Seng futures pointed to a firmer start before the bell. That early optimism faded as investors weighed the impact of higher global interest rates, oil prices near $106 a barrel and fresh Middle East tensions after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, according to regional market reports.

A sharp sell-off in South Korea also weighed on regional technology shares. Seoul's Kospi plunged 3.65% after Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies, known as CXMT, reported progress on a next-generation DRAM design. The news hit Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix and spilled over into chip and AI-related names across Asia.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank stock gets planned insider buying
sum: Shanghai Pudong Development Bank said on October 30, 2026, that senior executives, business directors and other core management personnel plan to increase their holdings of the bank's A-shares by using their own funds. The announcement was reported by Futubull.

The group includes heads of selected head-office departments, tier-one branches and subsidiaries. The planned purchases will be carried out through centralized bidding on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, beginning November 2, 2026, and continuing within a six-month window.

The planned buying gives investors a direct signal of management alignment, although it does not determine the eventual size or timing of individual transactions. The announcement also comes as the bank's third-quarter results and recent analyst assessments put earnings momentum and asset quality in focus.

A CICC analysis published on November 1 said third-quarter revenue rose 6.3 percent year over year and net profit attributable to shareholders increased 5.9 percent. The analysis also noted a quarter-on-quarter decline in the non-performing loan ratio to 1.24 percent at the end of the third quarter.

For investors, the next relevant signals are the execution of the planned purchases and the bank's progress in maintaining earnings growth while managing credit risk. The purchase plan is an announced intention rather than evidence that all transactions have already been completed.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank is a China-based commercial bank headquartered in Shanghai, serving individual and corporate customers. Its activities include deposits, personal lending, wealth management, cash management, supply-chain finance, trade finance, asset custody, investment banking and treasury services, according to the company profile and the bank's investor-relations site. The bank competes with other Chinese joint-stock commercial banks including China Merchants Bank, Industrial Bank and China CITIC Bank. Its profile is therefore that of a diversified national banking platform rather than a narrowly focused lender.
Investors can follow broader developments through current market reports.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank stock tracks stronger Q3 earnings
sum: Shanghai Pudong Development Bank reported stronger earnings for the third quarter and the first nine months of 2026, according to Futubull. Operating revenue for the first three quarters reached RMB 138.133 billion, up 4.42 percent year on year, while attributable net profit rose 4.52 percent to RMB 40.572 billion.

Third-quarter operating revenue increased 6.32 percent year on year to RMB 44.356 billion. Attributable net profit reached RMB 9.621 billion, a 5.93 percent increase from the same period a year earlier. Futubull also noted that third-quarter profit was below the second-quarter figure, indicating that year-on-year growth did not translate into sequential earnings expansion.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank shares were quoted at 10.02 CNY on the Shanghai market at 08:00 CET on Friday, October 30, 2026. The quote provides the latest available market reference for the Shanghai-listed instrument and is separate from the bank's earnings announcement.

The results give investors two signals to track: improving revenue growth through the first nine months and continued pressure to convert that growth into stronger quarterly momentum. For a commercial bank, the next focus will be the development of deposits, lending and asset quality as the year progresses.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank is headquartered in Shanghai, according to its investor-relations page. Its reported operations include deposits, loans and group subsidiaries, placing it in China's commercial banking sector. The bank operates alongside domestic joint-stock peers such as China Merchants Bank and Industrial Bank, competing for corporate, retail and financial-services business.

Visa Supports Chinese Cardholders to Add Cards to Apple Pay for a More Convenient and Secure Payment Experience
sum: SINGAPORE, Jan. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, Visa, a world leader in digital payments, announced its support for Chinese Visa cardholders to pay with Apple Pay. Together with Apple, Visa will enable Chinese cardholders to add Visa cards[1] from participating banks to Apple Pay and make payments at overseas Visa-accepting merchants, in-store, in-app and online. Today, 79 percent[2] of in-person transactions globally are made contactlessly with NFC.

Yin Xiaolong, General Manager at Visa Mainland China, said: "As global digital payments develop rapidly, consumers increasingly expect mobile payment solutions that are smartphone-based and interoperable. Visa has long been committed to providing Chinese cardholders with diverse payment options, enabling them to enjoy a secure and seamless payment experience wherever they are. Upholding our long‑standing commitment to the Chinese market and to our cardholders, Visa is increasing its investments in data and payment security, launching tokenization services and taking the lead in enabling their use in cross‑border scenarios. We are delighted to work with Apple and financial institutions to bring Chinese cardholders a safer and more convenient new mobile payment experience."

The first batch of supporting issuing banks includes Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Bank of China, Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of Communications, China Merchants Bank, China CITIC Bank, Ping An Bank and Industrial Bank. Visa and Apple are working closely with more banking partners, including Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, China Construction Bank, China Minsheng Bank and China Everbright Bank, and related features will be rolled out in the future.

When using Apple Pay for in-store payments, consumers simply double-click the side button, authenticate, and hold their iPhone or Apple Watch near the payment terminal for contactless payment. Every Apple Pay transaction requires secure authentication using Face ID, Touch ID, or device passcode, and the result is sent to the issuing bank as a one-time dynamic security transaction code, putting transaction security firmly in the hands of the consumer.
